newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent renews slide as gas oil falls below $166.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent renews slide as gas oil falls below $166.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures slipped further on Thursday due to an aggressive bout of selling in the gas oil pit which pushed prices under $166 a tonne on June.
July Brent was down 28 cents at $18.44 at 1145 GMT having peaked at $18.78 soon after the open and then dipped to a low of $18.39.
"There was one broker selling agressively on gas oil that pushed it down," said a broker
Other dealers said the market looked technically weak with support at $18.65 and $18.50 and some saw a soggy outlook for the physical market.
There was little fresh news after Wednesday's renewal of Iraq's oil-for-food deal.
IPE gas oil was down $2.75 cents a tonne at $166 at 1143 GMT having briefly hit $165.75. But analysts saw robust technical support in the area $160 to $165 a widely traded range in April.
Physical markets were also under pressure with Rotterdam barges talked under $1 a tonne above futures.
U.S. gasoline demand has failed to lift the wider market this week and many expected the weight of other oil products in the West to soon pressure crude prices.
A bearish set of U.S. stock figures earlier this week added to downward pressure and dealers now await an outlook on world oil markets from the International Energy Agency on Friday.
